ITQAN:v4p388/r23.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v4p388/r23.speaker: author
ITQAN:v4p388/r23.claim: The two men are Tamlikha, the good one, and Fitrus; the source identifies them with the pair mentioned in al-Saffat.
ITQAN:v4p388/r23.anchor: هما تمليخا وهو الخير وفطروس وهما المذكوران في سورة الصافات

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p172/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p172/r1.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p172/r1.claim: The verb ḥaffahu means to surround something on its sides; the cited line uses it of a ridge's flanks surrounding a following object.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p172/r1.anchor: حفه: طاف به من جوانبه. قال الشاعر:

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p172/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p172/r2.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p172/r2.claim: The related forms mean to make something surround another or for people to gather around its sides.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p172/r2.anchor: وخففته به: جعلته مطيفا به، وحف به القوم صاروا في حفته

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p172/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p172/r3.speaker: البصريون
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p172/r3.claim: Basran grammarians treat kullatā as singular in form but dual in meaning; its tāʾ replaces a wāw except in al-Jarmī's analysis, and its alif marks femininity.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p172/r3.anchor: كلتا: اسم مفرد اللفظ عند البصريين مثنى المعنى

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p172/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p172/r4.speaker: البغداديون
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p172/r4.claim: Baghdadian grammarians treat kullatā as dual in both form and meaning.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p172/r4.anchor: مثنى لفظا، ومعنى عند البغداديين وتاؤه عند البصريين

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p172/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p172/r5.speaker: الجرمي
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p172/r5.claim: Al-Jarmī instead treats the alif as additional and the word as having the pattern faʿīl.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p172/r5.anchor: غير الجرمي بدل من واو فأصله كلوى

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p174/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p174/r1.speaker: الزمخشري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p174/r1.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī describes two vineyards ringed by palms, a favored arrangement in which fruit trees enclose the vines.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p174/r1.anchor: وقال الزمخشري: جنتين من أعناب بساتين من كروم، وحففناهما بنخل

ASAD-NOTES:18:intro/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:18:intro/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:18:intro/r1.claim: The surah's parables contrast faith in God with undue attachment to worldly life; its key idea is that earthly beauty tests people, most clearly in the rich and poor men story.
ASAD-NOTES:18:intro/r1.anchor: and the key-phrase of the whole surah is the statement in verse 7,

STUDYQURAN:18:intro/r3.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:18:intro/r3.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:18:intro/r3.claim: The sūrah has three main narratives—the cave youths, Moses and the mysterious servant, and Dhu’l-Qarnayn—and a long parable warning against worldly enjoyment without gratitude and concern for the Hereafter.
STUDYQURAN:18:intro/r3.anchor: This sūrah contains three main narratives—that of the inhabitants of the cave

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:18:32/r1.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:18:32/r1.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:18:32/r1.claim: After describing the afterlife of believers and unbelievers, God gives two men as representatives: a wealthy unbeliever boasts, rejects resurrection, and expects an even better afterlife; his poor believing friend urges gratitude and warns that denying the afterlife amounts to denying God. Wealth and poverty are tests, shown through vivid contrast.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:18:32/r1.anchor: biri imanın, diğeri küfrün temsilcisi durumundaki iki adamın inanç ve davranış özelliklerini örnek vermiştir.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:18:32/r2.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:18:32/r2.speaker: tefsirlerde bir görüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:18:32/r2.claim: One identification makes the men two Meccan brothers from the Makhzum clan: unbeliever Aswad b. Abd al-Ashad and Muslim Abu Salama; their gardens were probably in Taif.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:18:32/r2.anchor: Bunlar Mekke’de Mahzûm kabilesinden iki kardeştir. Biri kâfir olan Esved b. Abdü’l-Eşed, diğeri ise müslüman olan kardeşi Ebû Seleme’dir.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:18:32/r3.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:18:32/r3.speaker: tefsirlerde bir görüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:18:32/r3.claim: A second identification makes them two Israelite brothers: one spent his inheritance on good causes, while the other bought the gardens in the parable and ultimately lost.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:18:32/r3.anchor: Bunlar İsrâiloğulları’ndan iki kardeştir. Babalarından kalan mirası bölüştüklerinde, mümin olan malını hayır yolunda harcamış

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:18:32/r4.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:18:32/r4.speaker: İbn Âşûr
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:18:32/r4.claim: A third view treats the story as a parable of believers’ security and unbelievers’ anxiety, portraying wealthy Meccan polytheists and poor Muslims; its placement warns that rich polytheists may meet the garden owner’s fate.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:18:32/r4.anchor: Bu olay inananla inanmayan insanın iç dünyalarını anlatan bir temsildir. Burada inanmanın insan ruhuna verdiği güven ve huzur

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.claim: The two-person parable exposes opponents who take worldly success as proof of their beliefs, infer that the afterlife is imaginary, or expect to fare better there than believers.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.anchor: they regarded their worldly success to be proof of the veracity of their ideology and deeds; when Muslims would warn them of God and the Hereafter, they would reply that since they were better off than them in worldly affairs

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.claim: The parable mirrors Quraysh’s outward and inward arrogance and the conflict between truth and falsehood; the poor companion has faith and joy in knowing God despite lacking orchards.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.anchor: The arrogant among the Quraysh are narrated a parable here which mirrors their inner and outer selves and also makes them see the fate of the conflict between truth and falsehood

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.claim: Giving the affluent man two orchards rather than one signifies the completion of God’s favour, as do the two gardens promised in al-Raḥmān.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.anchor: The fact that one of them was given two and not one orchard is to express the completion of favour on him by God. In S ūrah al-Ra ḥmān too it is mentioned that the dwellers of Paradise will be given two orchards.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.claim: An ideal Arab orchard had grapes, fruit-bearing date palms for beauty and shelter from hot winds, seasonal farmland, and a central stream with tributaries watering it.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.anchor: For the Arabs, the concept of an ideal orchard was one which was of grapes; its borders have date-palms that bear fruit, enhance the splendour of the orchard and protect it from sizzling winds.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.claim: The orchard owner arrogantly thought his lush garden indestructible, while Dhū al-Qarnayn is the grateful servant who credits his achievement to God and remembers God’s certain promise.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.anchor: the mentality of one of them was inflicted with arrogance: when he entered enter his lush orchard, he would haughtily say that he does not think that it will ever be destroyed.

BURSEVI:v5p189#2/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p189#2/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p189#2/r1.claim: The parable is directed to unbelievers immersed in blessings and believers enduring poverty, and concerns two men, perhaps brothers from Israel.
BURSEVI:v5p189#2/r1.anchor: وبين للكافرين المتقلبين في نعم الله والمؤمنين المكابدين لمشاق الفقر

BURSEVI:v5p189#2/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p189#2/r2.speaker: الجلالين
BURSEVI:v5p189#2/r2.claim: Al-Jalalayn identifies the two as sons of a king among the Israelites.
BURSEVI:v5p189#2/r2.anchor: قال في الجلالين : يريد ابني ملك كان في بني إسرائيل

BURSEVI:v5p189#2/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p189#2/r3.speaker: أبو حيان
BURSEVI:v5p189#2/r3.claim: Abu Hayyan infers from the term companion that the two men were not brothers.
BURSEVI:v5p189#2/r3.anchor: قال أبو حيان ويظهر من قوله : {فقال لصاحبه} أنه ليس أخاه

BURSEVI:v5p189#2/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p189#2/r4.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p189#2/r4.claim: The author rejects Abu Hayyan's inference: a brother can be called a companion, and the later scene of a man taking his brother through the garden supports their being siblings.
BURSEVI:v5p189#2/r4.anchor: التعبير عنهما برجلين يصحح إطلاق الصاحب على الأخ

BURSEVI:v5p189#2/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p189#2/r5.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p189#2/r5.claim: The account names the believing brother Yahuda and the unbeliever Qutrus; after inheriting eight thousand dinars, the believer gave his half away for heavenly land, a home, spouses, and servants, then became poor and was refused help.
BURSEVI:v5p189#2/r5.anchor: كان أحد الأخوين مؤمنا واسمه يهودا والآخر كافرا واسمه قطروس

BURSEVI:v5p189#2/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p189#2/r6.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p189#2/r6.claim: The two grape gardens are vineyards by metonymy or an ellipsis for grape trees; palms surround them and crops between them make a well ordered, productive whole.
BURSEVI:v5p189#2/r6.anchor: ليكون كل منهما جامعا للأقوات والفواكه متواصل العمارة

ALUSI-FULL:v15p273/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p273/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v15p273/r1.claim: The example addresses believers who worship morning and evening and unbelievers demanding their expulsion.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p273/r1.anchor: ( واضرب لهم ( للمؤمنين الذين يدعون ربهم بالغداة والعشي

ALUSI-FULL:v15p273/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p273/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v15p273/r2.claim: The two objects are the two men, with the second needing exposition; they may be hypothetical, but al-Ālūsī favors historicity.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p273/r2.anchor: مفعولان لا ضرب ثانيهما أولهما لأنه المحتاج إلى التفصيل

ALUSI-FULL:v15p273/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p273/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
ALUSI-FULL:v15p273/r3.claim: One account identifies Israelite brothers: the unbeliever Fartūs or Quṭfayr and the believer Judah.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p273/r3.anchor: فقيل هما أخوان من بني إسرائيل أحدهما كافر اسمه فرطوس وقيل اسمه قطفير والآخر مؤمن اسمه يهوذا في قول ابن عباس

ALUSI-FULL:v15p273/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p273/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
ALUSI-FULL:v15p273/r5.claim: Another account makes them sons of an Israelite king: one spent wealth for God, while the other disbelieved and pursued worldly adornment.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p273/r5.anchor: وعن ابن عباس أنهما ابنا ملك من بني إسرائيل أنفق أحدهما ماله

ALUSI-FULL:v15p273/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p273/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v15p273/r6.claim: A narrative says they were blacksmiths or inherited and divided eight thousand dinars; the believer spent his share seeking heavenly gardens, a home, spouses, and immortal youths, then became needy and was rejected by his brother.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p273/r6.anchor: وروي أنهما كانا حدادين كسبا مالا وروي أنهما ورثا من أبيهما ثماني آلاف دينار

ALUSI-FULL:v15p273/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p273/r7.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v15p273/r7.claim: A different identification makes them Banū Makhzūm: al-Aswad ibn al-Asad and Abū Salama ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAbd al-Asad.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p273/r7.anchor: وقيل هما أخوان من بني مخزوم كافر هو الأسود بن الأسد والمؤمن هو أبو سلمة عبدالله

ALUSI-FULL:v15p273/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p273/r8.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v15p273/r8.claim: The parable contrasts disobedience amid divine favors with obedience amid poverty, rather than repeating the previously described afterlife outcomes.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p273/r8.anchor: بل من حيث عصيان الكفرة مع تقلبهم في نعم الله تعالى وطاعة المؤمنين

ALUSI-FULL:v15p273/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p273/r9.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v15p273/r9.claim: The gardens’ location is unspecified because identifying it adds no significant benefit.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p273/r9.anchor: لم يتعين سبحانه مكانهما إذ لا يتعلق بتعيينه كبير فائدة

ALUSI-FULL:v15p273/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p273/r10.speaker: إبراهيم بن القاسم الكاتب
ALUSI-FULL:v15p273/r10.claim: Ibrāhīm ibn al-Qāsim’s Wonders of Lands says Lake Tinnīs was the site of the gardens, divided by God in one night.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p273/r10.anchor: وذكر إبراهيم بن القاسم الكاتب في كتابه عجائب البلاد أن بحيرة تينس

ALUSI-FULL:v15p273/r11.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p273/r11.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v15p273/r11.claim: A garden of grapes means vineyards, either by implied addition or figuratively; al-Rāghib says the word can denote fruit and vine.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p273/r11.anchor: من أعناب ( من كروم متنوعة فالكلام على ما قيل

ALUSI-FULL:v15p273/r12.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p273/r12.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v15p273/r12.claim: Palms surrounded and framed the vineyards; the bāʾ supplies a second object, and crops between the gardens joined staple foods with fruits.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p273/r12.anchor: وحففناهما بنخل ( أي جعلنا النخل محيطة بهما

ALUSI-FULL:v15p309#2/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p309#2/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v15p309#2/r3.claim: The two-men parable consoles poor people relying on God and warns wealthy people deluded by riches.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p309#2/r3.anchor: الخ فيه من تسلية الفقراء المتوكلين على الله تعالى وتنبيه الاغنياء المغرورين

ALUSI-FULL:v15p309#2/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p309#2/r4.speaker: النيسابوري
ALUSI-FULL:v15p309#2/r4.claim: Al-Nīsābūrī identifies the two men as the unbelieving self and believing heart; the gardens are desire and world, grapes lusts, palms leadership, crops animal pleasures, and river human faculties and senses.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p309#2/r4.anchor: وقال النيسابوري الرجلان هما النفس الكافرة والقلب المؤمن

ALUSI-FULL:v15p309#2/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p309#2/r5.speaker: النيسابوري
ALUSI-FULL:v15p309#2/r5.claim: Al-Nīsābūrī reads the gardens as desire and world, fruit as cravings, boasting of wealth and status as inclination and blameworthy traits, expecting a better garden as delusion about God, and turning hands over as regret for wasted life and good potential.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p309#2/r5.anchor: قال ذلك غرورا بالله تعالى وكرمه

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p169/r8.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p169/r8.speaker: قيل
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p169/r8.claim: A report says the parable concerns two Meccan brothers of Banu Makhzum: the believer Abu Salama and the unbeliever al-Aswad ibn Abd al-Asad.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p169/r8.anchor: قيل: نزلت في أخوين من أهل مكة من بني مخزوم أحدهما مؤمن وهو أبو سلمة

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p170#2/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p170#2/r1.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p170#2/r1.claim: The example asks the audience to recall the story of two men; one received two vineyards.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p170#2/r1.anchor: {واضرب لهم مثلا رجلين} اذكر لهم خبر رجلين {جعلنا لأحدهما جنتين} بستانين

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p170#2/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p170#2/r2.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p170#2/r2.claim: The gardens were ringed with palms; ḥifāf means the side and ḥafafa describes people surrounding something.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p170#2/r2.anchor: {من أعناب وحففناهما بنخل} أي: أطفناهما من جوانبهما بنخل والحفاف: الجانب وجمعه أحفة

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p170#2/r3.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p170#2/r3.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p170#2/r3.claim: Crops were placed around the vineyards and palms in their middle.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p170#2/r3.anchor: {وجعلنا بينهما زرعا} أي: جعلنا حول الأعناب النخيل ووسط الأعناب الزرع.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p170#2/r4.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p170#2/r4.speaker: قيل
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p170#2/r4.claim: Alternatively, crops lay between the two gardens, so there was no uncultivated patch between them.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p170#2/r4.anchor: وقيل: "بينهما" أي بين الجنتين زرعا يعني: لم يكن بين الجنتين موضع خراب.

BAYDAWI-FULL:18:32/r1.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:18:32/r1.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:18:32/r1.claim: The parable is for disbeliever and believer; one account identifies Israelite brothers Qatrus and Judah, who split an inheritance of 8,000 dinars: one bought estates while the other spent on good works.
BAYDAWI-FULL:18:32/r1.anchor: هما أخوان من بني إسرائيل كافر اسمه قطروس ومؤمن اسمه يهوذا، ورثا من أبيهما ثمانية آلاف دينار

BAYDAWI-FULL:18:32/r2.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:18:32/r2.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:18:32/r2.claim: Another identification makes them brothers from Banu Makhzum: unbeliever al-Aswad ibn Abd al-Asad and believer Abu Salama Abd Allah, later husband of Umm Salama before the Prophet.
BAYDAWI-FULL:18:32/r2.anchor: وقيل الممثل بهما أخوان من بني مخزوم كافر وهو الأسود بن عبد الأشد

BAYDAWI-FULL:18:32/r3.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:18:32/r3.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:18:32/r3.claim: The gardens are two grape orchards, and the complete phrase explains the parable or describes the men.
BAYDAWI-FULL:18:32/r3.anchor: من كروم والجملة بتمامها بيان للتمثيل أو صفة للرجلين

BAYDAWI-FULL:18:32/r4.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:18:32/r4.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:18:32/r4.claim: Date palms surrounded the grape gardens; grammatically the bā gives the verb a second object.
BAYDAWI-FULL:18:32/r4.anchor: وجعلنا النخل محيطة بهما مؤزرا بها كرومهما

BAYDAWI-FULL:18:32/r5.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:18:32/r5.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:18:32/r5.claim: Crops between the gardens made each orchard supply both staples and fruits, with continuous cultivation arranged beautifully.
BAYDAWI-FULL:18:32/r5.anchor: ليكون كل منهما جامعا للأقوات والفواكه متواصل العمارة

BIQAI-FULL:v4p444/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v4p444/r3.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v4p444/r3.claim: The two-garden story concerns two Israelites: one is deceived by wealth and assumes permanence, while his believing companion relies on God; the garden disappears and regret remains.
BIQAI-FULL:v4p444/r3.anchor: وقد أفصحت هذه الآي منها باغترار أحدهما بما لديه وركونه إلى توهم البقاء

BIQAI-FULL:v4p444/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v4p444/r4.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v4p444/r4.claim: The ruined garden illustrates that whoever relies on anything besides God loses it, since everything perishes except Him.
BIQAI-FULL:v4p444/r4.anchor: وهذه حال من ركن إلى ما سوى المالك , ومن كل شيء إلا وجهه سبحانه وتعالى فان وهالك

BIQAI-FULL:v4p445/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v4p445/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v4p445/r1.claim: The stories reproach Israelites for delaying faith and presuming their answers to Quraysh made them uniquely knowledgeable; Moses and Khidr's story calls them to submit to God's encompassing knowledge.
BIQAI-FULL:v4p445/r1.anchor: وفي كل ذلك من تأديب بني إسرائيل وتقريعهم وتوبيخ مرتكبهم في توقفهم عن الإيمان

BIQAI-FULL:v4p466/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v4p466/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v4p466/r1.claim: The parable addresses poor believers and arrogant opponents demanding their expulsion: worldly comfort is temporary and cannot justify pride or ingratitude.
BIQAI-FULL:v4p466/r1.anchor: فاعتمدوا عليهم وركنوا إليه ولم يشكروا من آتاهم إياه عليه , بل أداهم إلى الافتقار

BIQAI-FULL:v4p466/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v4p466/r2.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v4p466/r2.claim: The gardens may lie on different terrain, such as plain and mountain, so one common calamity of heat or cold would not strike both alike.
BIQAI-FULL:v4p466/r2.anchor: ومن جملة الأوضاع أن تكون إحداهما من السهل والأخرى في الجبل , ليبعد عموم عاهة

BIQAI-FULL:v4p466/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v4p466/r3.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v4p466/r3.claim: Grapevines thrive in cold regions yet tolerate heat and provide fruit, staple food, raisins, and vinegar.
BIQAI-FULL:v4p466/r3.anchor: من أعناب } لأنها من أشجار البلاد الباردة وتصبر على الحر , وهي فاكهة وقوت

BIQAI-FULL:v4p466/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v4p466/r4.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v4p466/r4.claim: Palm trees thrive in hot regions yet tolerate cold, may protect grapes from some calamities, and provide fruit and staple dates.
BIQAI-FULL:v4p466/r4.anchor: بنخل } لأنها من أشجار البلاد الحارة , وتصبر على البرد , وربما منعت عن الأعناب

BIQAI-FULL:v4p466/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v4p466/r5.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v4p466/r5.claim: The palms form a beautiful, useful crown around the grapes, a prized arrangement for landowners.
BIQAI-FULL:v4p466/r5.anchor: فكأن النخل كالإكليل من وراء العنب , وهو مما يؤثره الدهاقين لأنه في غاية البهجة والمنفعة

BIQAI-FULL:v4p466/r6.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v4p466/r6.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v4p466/r6.claim: Grain between the gardens reduces the chance that one blight ruins all, supplies prime staple food, and keeps the extensive land continuously cultivated.
BIQAI-FULL:v4p466/r6.anchor: لبعد شمول الآفة للكل , لأن زمان الزرع ومكانه غير زمان أثمار الشجر المقدم وأفضل الأقوات

DURR-FULL:v5p388/r11.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p388/r11.speaker: السدي رضي الله عنه
DURR-FULL:v5p388/r11.claim: The two gardens were one orchard enclosed by a single wall, with a river between the sides; each side was named for its bordering wall.
DURR-FULL:v5p388/r11.anchor: عن السدي رضي الله عنه في قوله: {جعلنا لأحدهما جنتين من أعناب} قال: إن الجنة هي البستان

QUSHAYRI:v2p220/r2.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v2p220/r2.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v2p220/r2.claim: Outwardly, one of two garden owners thanked his Creator while the other disbelieved his Provider; the latter's garden was ruined and he regretted neglecting gratitude.
QUSHAYRI:v2p220/r2.anchor: فشكر أحدهما لخالقه وكفر الآخر برازقه

QUSHAYRI:v2p220/r3.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v2p220/r3.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v2p220/r3.claim: In the inward reading, two servants are granted ease and divine gentleness; one advances through the stations from good beginnings toward completion.
QUSHAYRI:v2p220/r3.anchor: يخلق عبدين يطيب لهما الوقت ، ويمهد لهما بساط اللطف

QUSHAYRI:v2p220/r4.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v2p220/r4.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v2p220/r4.claim: The successful servant's struggle yields good character, then pure spiritual states, and finally self-annihilation in the realities of divine unity.
QUSHAYRI:v2p220/r4.anchor: فتميز له المجاهدة ثمرات أحسن الأخلاق

QUSHAYRI:v2p220/r5.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v2p220/r5.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v2p220/r5.claim: The second servant undervalues the good beginning, returns to habits, abandons the path, and falls into heedlessness, separation, expulsion, humiliation, and estrangement.
QUSHAYRI:v2p220/r5.anchor: فيرتد عن سلوك الطريقة ويتردى في ظلمة الغفلة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p316/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p316/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p316/r1.claim: Ibn Ashur speculates the gardens may have been near Taif, where Meccans had orchards.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p316/r1.anchor: ولم يذكر المفسرون أين كانت الجنتان ، ولعلهما كانتا بالطائف

IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p316/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p316/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p316/r2.claim: Ibn Abbas says the two men were Israelite brothers who inherited money: one bought land and built gardens, while the other gave his wealth away.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p316/r2.anchor: وعن ابن عباس : هما أخوان من بني إسرائيل مات أبوهما وترك لهما مالا

IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p316/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p316/r3.speaker: ابن عطية
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p316/r3.claim: Some commentators cited by Ibn Atiyya treat the pair as an imagined case; this would be a vivid comparison of one conceivable state with another, like the garden parable in al-Baqara.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p316/r3.anchor: وإن كان حال الرجلين حالا مفروضا كما جوزه بعض المفسرين فيما نقله عنه ابن عطية

IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p316/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p316/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p316/r4.claim: The narrative is more likely historical: its unprefixed dialogue and the later report of the man's defeat resemble remembered events and make the warning more forceful.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p316/r4.anchor: والأظهر من سياق الكلام وصنع التراكيب مثل قوله : قال له صاحبه وهو يحاوره

IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p316/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p316/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p316/r5.claim: Ja'alna means that God determined the means for the gardens; the vocabulary recalls the garden of palms and grapes in al-Baqara.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p316/r5.anchor: ومعنى جعلنا لأحدهما } قدرنا له أسباب ذلك

IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p316/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p316/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p316/r6.claim: Hafafna means surrounded; gardens are enhanced when encircled by fruit trees, as the same root describes angels around the Throne.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p316/r6.anchor: ومعنى حففناهما } أحطناهما ، يقال : حفه بكذا

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p515#2/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p515#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p515#2/r1.claim: The parable addresses the arrogant group seeking to dismiss poor believers and those believers; owners represent a Qurayshi/Tamīmī notable and Bilāl, ʿAmmār, Ṣuhayb, and peers.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p515#2/r1.anchor: الضمير في لهم عائد على الطائفة المتجبرة

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p515#2/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p515#2/r2.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p515#2/r2.claim: Ḥaffafnāhumā means palms surrounded the gardens on every side; ḥifāf can mean a couch or furrow's side.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p515#2/r2.anchor: وحففناهما بمعنى وجعلنا ذلك لها من كل جهة

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p138#2/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p138#2/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p138#2/r1.claim: Ata reports from Ibn Abbas that the two men were sons of an Israelite king: one built gardens and palaces, while the other was ascetic and spent matching wealth on his afterlife; they exemplify believer and arrogant unbeliever.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p138#2/r1.anchor: هما ابنا ملك كان في بني اسرائيل توفي وتركهما فاتخذ أحدهما الجنان والقصور وكان الآخر زاهدا في الدنيا

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p138#2/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p138#2/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p138#2/r2.claim: Abu Salih reports that the needy Muslim told his unbelieving brother he had spent their inheritance for God’s cause; the brother invested his share in gardens and livestock, refused help unless he joined his religion, and displayed the estate.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p138#2/r2.anchor: ان المسلم لما احتاج تعرض لأخيه الكافر فقال الكافر اين ما ورثت عن ابيك فقال انفقته في سبيل الله

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p138#2/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p138#2/r3.speaker: مقاتل
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p138#2/r3.claim: Muqatil names the believer Yamlīkha and the unbeliever Qurtus, also called Qatras.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p138#2/r3.anchor: اسم المؤمن يمليخا واسم الكافر قرطس وقيل قطرس

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p138#2/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p138#2/r4.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p138#2/r4.claim: Another view takes the parable to concern ʿUyayna ibn Hisn and his companions, and Salman and his companions.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p138#2/r4.anchor: وقيل هذا المثل ضرب لعيينة بن حصن واصحابه ولسلمان واصحابه

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p138#2/r5.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p138#2/r5.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p138#2/r5.claim: Ḥaff means encircling; the palms surrounded the vineyards, and the crop between them signals that the gardens were fully cultivated.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p138#2/r5.anchor: الحف الاحاطة بالشيء ومنه قوله حافين من حول العرش الزمر 75

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p157/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p157/r1.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p157/r1.claim: The parable addresses arrogant polytheists who rejected sitting with poor Muslims and boasted of wealth and lineage; God gives one man two productive grape gardens surrounded by palms with crops between.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p157/r1.anchor: يقول الله تعالى بعد ذكر (1) المشركين المستكبرين عن مجالسة (2) الضعفاء والمساكين من المسلمين، وافتخروا عليهم بأموالهم وأحسابهم،

JISHUMI:v6p4407/r13.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v6p4407/r13.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v6p4407/r13.claim: Ḥaffa means to surround; ḥifāf means two sides.
JISHUMI:v6p4407/r13.anchor: حفوا بالشيء: أطافوا به، ومنه: (حافين من حول العرش). وحفاف كل شيء: جانباه،

JISHUMI:v6p4409/r7.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v6p4409/r7.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v6p4409/r7.claim: One occasion identifies two Meccan brothers of Banu Makhzum: believer Abu Salama and unbeliever al-Aswad.
JISHUMI:v6p4409/r7.anchor: قيل: نزلت في أخوين من أهل مكة من بني مخزوم مؤمنين، وهو: أبو سلمة عبد الله بن عبد الأسد

JISHUMI:v6p4409/r8.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v6p4409/r8.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v6p4409/r8.claim: Another view says the parable concerns the Prophet and Meccan polytheists.
JISHUMI:v6p4409/r8.anchor: وقيل: نزلت في رسول الله - صلى الله عليه وسلم - وفي مشركي مكة.

JISHUMI:v6p4409/r9.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v6p4409/r9.speaker: ابن عباس
JISHUMI:v6p4409/r9.claim: A report compares Uyayna and his companions with Salman and his companions, like two Israelite brothers; Ibn Abbas names the believer Judah.
JISHUMI:v6p4409/r9.anchor: وقيل: هذا مثل لعيينة بن حصين وأصحابه مع سلمان وأصحابه، شبههما برجلين من بني إسرائيل أخوين أحدهما مؤمن اسمه يهوذا، عن ابن عباس،

JISHUMI:v6p4409/r10.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v6p4409/r10.speaker: مقاتل
JISHUMI:v6p4409/r10.claim: Another report names the believing brother Tamlikha and the unbeliever Qatrus.
JISHUMI:v6p4409/r10.anchor: وقيل: اسمه: تمليخا، عن مقاتل، والآخر كافر اسمه: قطروس

JISHUMI:v6p4409/r11.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v6p4409/r11.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v6p4409/r11.claim: The brothers inherited wealth; one spent it for God while the other mocked him. The story is connected with 37:50.
JISHUMI:v6p4409/r11.anchor: فكانت قصتهما أنهما كانا أخوين ورثا مالا، فأنفق المؤمن من ماله في سبيل الله

JISHUMI:v6p4409/r12.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v6p4409/r12.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v6p4409/r12.claim: The parable contrasts the poor believer, honored with God, and the rich unbeliever, despite his wealth.
JISHUMI:v6p4409/r12.anchor: ليعلموا حال المؤمن وأنه جمع فقره عند الله وجيه، والكافر مع كثرة ماله مهان

JISHUMI:v6p4409/r13.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v6p4409/r13.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v6p4409/r13.claim: One interpretation places palms around vineyards and crops inside; another puts crops between the gardens, attributed to named authorities.
JISHUMI:v6p4409/r13.anchor: قيل: حول الأعناب النخل ووسط الأعناب الزرع، وقيل: بين الجنتين الزرع، عن الأصم، وأبي علي، وأبي مسلم.

AKHFASH:v2p430#2/r1.author: al-Akhfash al-Awsaṭ
AKHFASH:v2p430#2/r1.speaker: author
AKHFASH:v2p430#2/r1.claim: The parable mentions two men, but only one had fruit; mentioning both in the setup suffices for the singular وكان له ثمر.
AKHFASH:v2p430#2/r1.anchor: وقوله {واضرب لهم مثلا رجلين} وقال {وكان له ثمر} وإنما ذكر الرجلين في المعنى وكان لأحدهما ثمر

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p673#2/r1.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p673#2/r1.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p673#2/r1.claim: The parable compares unbelievers and believers with two brothers, one disbelieving and one believing.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p673#2/r1.anchor: أي ومثل حال الكافرين والمؤمنين ، بحال رجلين وكانا أخوين في بني إسرائيل

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p673#2/r2.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p673#2/r2.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p673#2/r2.claim: One account names the Israelite brothers Qatros, the unbeliever, and Yahudha, the believer; they inherited eight thousand dinars and divided it equally.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p673#2/r2.anchor: أحدهما كافر اسمه قطروس ، والآخر مؤمن اسمه يهوذا

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p673#2/r4.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p673#2/r4.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p673#2/r4.claim: In an illustrative story, the believing brother spends four thousand dinars on heavenly equivalents of land, home, spouse, and servants, donating each thousand; when needy he meets his wealthy brother, who rebukes and drives him away.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p673#2/r4.anchor: فاشترى الكافر أرضا بألف ، فقال المؤمن : اللهم إن أخي اشترى أرضا بألف دينار ، وأنا أشتري منك أرضا في الجنة بألف

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p673#2/r5.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p673#2/r5.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p673#2/r5.claim: An alternative identification makes the brothers Makhzumites: the believer is Abu Salama, later husband of Umm Salama before Muhammad, and the unbeliever is al-Aswad ibn Abd al-Asad.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p673#2/r5.anchor: مؤمن وهو أبو سلمة عبد الله بن عبد الأشد ، وكان زوج أم سلمة قبل رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p673#2/r6.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p673#2/r6.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p673#2/r6.claim: The two grape gardens are ringed by date palms with crops between them, an arrangement landowners use to border vineyards with fruit trees.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p673#2/r6.anchor: وحففناهما بنخل } وجعلنا النخل محيطا بالجنتين ، وهذا مما يؤثره الدهاقين في كرومهم

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p673#2/r7.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p673#2/r7.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p673#2/r7.claim: The construction describes one connected, carefully arranged estate of crops and fruit, with complete harvests and abundant river water.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p673#2/r7.anchor: ووصف العمارة بأنها متواصلة متشابكة لم يتوسطها ما يقطعها ويفصل بينها ، مع الشكل الحسن والترتيب الأنيق

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p305#2/r1.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p305#2/r1.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p305#2/r1.claim: A jannah is an orchard; combining grapes and palms with crops beneath makes the most beautiful and useful garden, with fruit above and crops below.
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p305#2/r1.anchor: الجنة : البستان , فإذا جمع العنب والنخل وكان تحتها زرع فهي أجمل الجنان وأجداها نفعا ,

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p305#2/r2.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p305#2/r2.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p305#2/r2.claim: The phrase about crops between the two gardens describes crops growing below their trees.
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p305#2/r2.anchor: لثمر أعاليها وزرع أسافلها ، وهو معنى قوله { وجعلنا بينهما رزعا } .

MUQATIL:18:32-33/r1.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:18:32-33/r1.speaker: author
MUQATIL:18:32-33/r1.claim: The likeness is a description for the people of Mecca; mathal means a likeness.
MUQATIL:18:32-33/r1.anchor: يعني وصف لهم، يعني لأهل مكة

MUQATIL:18:32-33/r2.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:18:32-33/r2.speaker: author
MUQATIL:18:32-33/r2.claim: The two brothers were Israelites: the believer was Yamlīkha, the unbeliever Firtas, and each inherited four thousand dinars from their father.
MUQATIL:18:32-33/r2.anchor: أحدهما مؤمن واسمه يمليخا، والآخر كافر، واسمه فرطس

MUQATIL:18:32-33/r3.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:18:32-33/r3.speaker: author
MUQATIL:18:32-33/r3.claim: The believer spent his inheritance on the poor, orphans, and needy; the unbeliever invested in houses, livestock, and gardens.
MUQATIL:18:32-33/r3.anchor: فعمد المؤمن فأنفق ماله على الفقراء واليتامى والمساكين

MUQATIL:18:32-33/r4.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:18:32-33/r4.speaker: author
MUQATIL:18:32-33/r4.claim: The unbelieving brother is the one given two gardens.
MUQATIL:18:32-33/r4.anchor: يعني الكافر، { جنتين من أعناب وحففناهما بنخل

NASAFI-FULL:v3p13/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p13/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p13/r1.claim: The parable compares disbelievers and believers through two men, identified as Israelite brothers: the unbeliever Qutrus and the Muslim Judah.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p13/r1.anchor: ومثل حال الكافرين والمؤمنين بحال رجلين وكانا أخوين في بني إسرائيل أحدهما كافر اسمه قطروس والآخر مسلم اسمه يهوذا

NASAFI-FULL:v3p13/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p13/r2.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p13/r2.claim: Another view identifies them with the companions mentioned in 37:51, including the speaker who says he had a companion.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p13/r2.anchor: وقيل هما المذكوران في والصافات في قوله قال قائل منهم اني كان لي قرين

NASAFI-FULL:v3p13/r3.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p13/r3.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p13/r3.claim: The brothers inherited eight thousand dinars and split it equally; the believer spent his share as charitable purchases of heavenly rewards while his brother acquired worldly goods.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p13/r3.anchor: ورثا من ابيهما ثمانية آلاف دينار فجعلاهما شطرين فاشترى الكافر أرضا بألف دينار فقال المؤمن اللهم إن أخي اشترى أرضا

NASAFI-FULL:v3p13/r4.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p13/r4.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p13/r4.claim: In the account, the believer gives the price of a house for a home in Paradise and turns his brother’s bridal payment into a dowry for heavenly maidens.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p13/r4.anchor: ثم بني أخوه دارا بألف فتصدق به ثم تزوج أخوه امرأة بألف فقال اللهم اني جعلت الفا صداقا للحور

NASAFI-FULL:v3p13/r5.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p13/r5.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p13/r5.claim: The believer also gives money for servants and goods in exchange for immortal youths; after becoming needy he approaches his brother, who rebukes and expels him.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p13/r5.anchor: ثم اشترى أخوه خدما ومتاعا بألف دينار فقال اللهم إني اشتريت منك الولدان المخلدين بألف فتصدق به ثم اصابته حاجة

NASAFI-FULL:v3p13/r6.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p13/r6.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p13/r6.claim: The two vineyards are surrounded by palms, an arrangement favored by landowners; حففته means encircling something, and the added ب makes the verb take a second object.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p13/r6.anchor: وحففناهما بنخل وجعلنا النخل محيطا بالجنتين وهذا مما يؤثره الدهاقين في كرومهم أن يجعلوها مؤزرة بالأشجار المثمرة

NASAFI-FULL:v3p13/r7.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p13/r7.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p13/r7.claim: The crop between the gardens makes the cultivated space continuous, interwoven, orderly, and pleasing, with nothing interrupting it.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p13/r7.anchor: جعلناها أرضا جامعة للأقوات والفواكه ووصف العمارة بأنها متواصلة متشابكة لم يتوسطها ما يقطعها

QURTUBI-FULL:18:32/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:18:32/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:18:32/r1.claim: The parable concerns those proud of worldly goods who disdain sitting with believers; it connects with the command to remain patient with believers.
QURTUBI-FULL:18:32/r1.anchor: هذا مثل لمن يتعزز بالدنيا ويستنكف عن مجالسة المؤمنين، وهو متصل بقوله { واصبر نفسك }.

QURTUBI-FULL:18:32/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:18:32/r2.speaker: الكلبي
QURTUBI-FULL:18:32/r2.claim: Al-Kalbi says it was revealed about Makhzumi brothers in Mecca: believer Abu Salama and unbeliever al-Aswad ibn Abd al-Asad; each inherited four thousand dinars, one spending his share for God.
QURTUBI-FULL:18:32/r2.anchor: فقال الكلبي: نزلت في أخوين من أهل مكة مخزوميين، أحدهما مؤمن وهو أبو سلمة عبد الله بن عبد الأسد

QURTUBI-FULL:18:32/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:18:32/r3.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:18:32/r3.claim: The brothers are linked to the companion in 37:51. Other identifications make the pair the Prophet and Meccans, all believers and disbelievers, or Uyayna's party against Salman and Suhayb.
QURTUBI-FULL:18:32/r3.anchor: وهما الأخوان المذكوران في سورة «الصافات» في قوله قال قآئل منهم إني كان لي قرين

QURTUBI-FULL:18:32/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:18:32/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
QURTUBI-FULL:18:32/r4.claim: Another account makes them Israelite brothers, with the believing brother named Judah according to Ibn Abbas and Tamlīkha according to Muqatil, and the unbeliever Qartush.
QURTUBI-FULL:18:32/r4.anchor: شبههم الله برجلين من بني إسرائيل أخوين أحدهما مؤمن واسمه يهوذا في قول ابن عباس.

QURTUBI-FULL:18:32/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:18:32/r5.speaker: مقاتل
QURTUBI-FULL:18:32/r5.claim: Muqatil names the brothers Tamlīkha and Qartush; one account says the believer freed slaves, clothed the naked, fed the hungry, and built mosques, while the other invested in worldly prosperity.
QURTUBI-FULL:18:32/r5.anchor: وقال مقاتل: اسمه تمليخا. والآخر كافر واسمه قرطوش.

QURTUBI-FULL:18:32/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:18:32/r6.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:18:32/r6.claim: The impoverished believer seeks work in the rich brother's garden; the rich man mocks his faith, denies resurrection, and expels him.
QURTUBI-FULL:18:32/r6.anchor: وأدركت الأول الحاجة، فأراد أن يستخدم نفسه في جنة يخدمها فقال: لو ذهبت لشريكي وصاحبي

QURTUBI-FULL:18:32/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:18:32/r7.speaker: عطاء
QURTUBI-FULL:18:32/r7.claim: Ata says the two men were partners who owned eight thousand dinars.
QURTUBI-FULL:18:32/r7.anchor: قال عطاء: كانا شريكين لهما ثمانية آلاف دينار.

QURTUBI-FULL:18:32-34/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:18:32-34/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:18:32-34/r1.claim: A further story has the poor brother spend his share on heavenly land, a house, a wife, and servants and goods; the rich brother rejects belief and worships an idol.
QURTUBI-FULL:18:32-34/r1.anchor: وقيل: ورثاه من أبيهما وكانا أخوين فاقتسماها، فاشترى أحدهما أرضا بألف دينار،

QURTUBI-FULL:18:32-34/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:18:32-34/r2.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:18:32-34/r2.claim: The brothers test their claims by fishing; the unbeliever catches many fish while invoking an idol, and the believer catches none while invoking God.
QURTUBI-FULL:18:32-34/r2.anchor: فقال: سر بنا نصطد السمك، فمن صاد أكثر فهو على حق فقال له: يا أخي!

QURTUBI-FULL:18:32-34/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:18:32-34/r3.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:18:32-34/r3.claim: The assigned angel protests; Gabriel shows each brother his Paradise or Hell home, and both judge worldly fortune irrelevant to that final destination.
QURTUBI-FULL:18:32-34/r3.anchor: قال: فضج الملك الموكل بهما، فأمر الله تعالى جبريل أن يأخذه فيذهب به إلى الجنان

QURTUBI-FULL:18:32-34/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:18:32-34/r4.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:18:32-34/r4.claim: God takes the believer and destroys the unbeliever; in Paradise the believer recalls his companion and asks to see him in Hell, echoing 37:51–52.
QURTUBI-FULL:18:32-34/r4.anchor: ثم إن الله تعالى توفى المؤمن وأهلك الكافر بعذاب من عنده، فلما استقر المؤمن في الجنة

QURTUBI-FULL:18:32-33/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:18:32-33/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:18:32-33/r1.claim: The present surah describes the brothers' worldly condition, while 37:51–61 describes their afterlife condition.
QURTUBI-FULL:18:32-33/r1.anchor: بين الله تعالى حال الأخوين في الدنيا في هذه السورة، وبين حالهما في الآخرة في سورة «الصافات»

QURTUBI-FULL:18:32-33/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:18:32-33/r2.speaker: ابن عطية
QURTUBI-FULL:18:32-33/r2.claim: Ibn Atiyya cites a report that Lake Tinnis was the gardens; one brother sold his share, spent in obedience, was mocked, and the lake flooded overnight.
QURTUBI-FULL:18:32-33/r2.anchor: قال ابن عطية: وذكر إبراهيم بن القاسم الكاتب في كتابه في عجائب البلاد أن بحيرة تنيس كانت هاتين الجنتين،

QURTUBI-FULL:18:32-33/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:18:32-33/r3.speaker: الماوردي
QURTUBI-FULL:18:32-33/r3.claim: Al-Mawardi says the story may be a parable for this community urging renunciation of worldly life and desire for the hereafter; Qurtubi says the context argues otherwise.
QURTUBI-FULL:18:32-33/r3.anchor: وقد قيل: إن هذا مثل ضربه الله تعالى لهذه الأمة، وليس بخبر عن حال متقدمة،

QURTUBI-FULL:18:32-33/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:18:32-33/r4.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:18:32-33/r4.claim: Palms surrounded the gardens, with crops among grapevines; حفاف means a side or encircling edge.
QURTUBI-FULL:18:32-33/r4.anchor: { وحففناهما بنخل } أي أطفناهما من جوانبهما بنخل. والحفاف الجانب،

QURTUBI-FULL:18:32-33/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:18:32-33/r5.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:18:32-33/r5.claim: كلتا means each garden; singular آتت supports the Basran view that كلا and كلتا are singular forms denoting a pair.
QURTUBI-FULL:18:32-33/r5.anchor: { كلتا الجنتين } أي كل واحدة من الجنتين { آتت أكلها } تاما، ولذلك لم يقل آتتا.

QURTUBI-FULL:18:32-33/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:18:32-33/r6.speaker: أهل البصرة
QURTUBI-FULL:18:32-33/r6.claim: Basrans treat كلا and كلتا as singular forms emphasizing two, inflected alike with an overt noun but changing alif to ya with a pronoun.
QURTUBI-FULL:18:32-33/r6.anchor: فقال أهل البصرة: هو مفرد لأن كلا وكلتا في توكيد الاثنين نظير «كل» في المجموع،

QURTUBI-FULL:18:32-33/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:18:32-33/r7.speaker: الفراء
QURTUBI-FULL:18:32-33/r7.claim: Al-Farra treats them as duals derived from كل by lightening lām and adding dual alif; they are always annexed and lack a standalone singular.
QURTUBI-FULL:18:32-33/r7.anchor: وقال الفراء: هو مثنى، وهو مأخوذ من كل فخففت اللام وزيدت الألف للتثنية.

QURTUBI-FULL:18:32-34#2/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:18:32-34#2/r1.speaker: أهل البصرة
QURTUBI-FULL:18:32-34#2/r1.claim: The Basrans reject the dual analysis because oblique inflection with an overt noun would require ya; the poet's shortened form is necessity, not proof.
QURTUBI-FULL:18:32-34#2/r1.anchor: وهذا القول ضعيف عند أهل البصرة لأنه لو كان مثنى لوجب أن تكون ألفه في النصب والجر ياء مع الاسم الظاهر،

QURTUBI-FULL:18:32-34#2/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:18:32-34#2/r2.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:18:32-34#2/r2.claim: Qurtubi concludes كلا is singular in form but denotes a specific pair, unlike كل which means comprehensive totality; نحن likewise has singular form but can refer to two or more.
QURTUBI-FULL:18:32-34#2/r2.anchor: فثبت أنه اسم مفرد كمعى، إلا أنه وضع ليدل على التثنية،

QURTUBI-FULL:18:32-34#2/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:18:32-34#2/r3.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:18:32-34#2/r3.claim: Jarir's line predicates a singular day of كلا, as the verse uses singular آتت; a true dual would require plural agreement.
QURTUBI-FULL:18:32-34#2/r3.anchor: يدل على ذلك قول جرير: كلا يومي أمامة يوم صد

QURTUBI-FULL:18:32-34#2/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:18:32-34#2/r4.speaker: سيبويه
QURTUBI-FULL:18:32-34#2/r4.claim: Sibawayh says the alif of كلتا marks femininity and tā replaces an original wāw; al-Jurmi instead makes tā augment and the alif root.
QURTUBI-FULL:18:32-34#2/r4.anchor: فقال سيبويه: ألف «كلتا» للتأنيث والتاء بدل من لام الفعل وهي واو

MAJAZ:v1p401/r2.author: Abū ʿUbayda Maʿmar b. al-Muthannā
MAJAZ:v1p401/r2.speaker: author
MAJAZ:v1p401/r2.claim: حففناهما means surrounded them from every side; al-Ṭirimmāḥ’s محفوفة illustrates the usage.
MAJAZ:v1p401/r2.anchor: «وحففناهما بنخل» (32) مجازه: أطفناهما وحجزناهما من جوانبهما

RAZI-FULL:v21p105/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p105/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v21p105/r1.claim: The parable answers disbelievers who boast of wealth and supporters over poor Muslims: fortunes can reverse, while true distinction lies in obedience to God.
RAZI-FULL:v21p105/r1.anchor: الكفار افتخروا بأموالهم وأنصارهم على فقراء المسلمين

RAZI-FULL:v21p105/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p105/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v21p105/r2.claim: One account makes the men Israelite brothers, Bratus and Judah, who inherited 8,000 dinars; the believer gave away his half seeking heavenly property while his brother bought land, a house, a wife, servants, and estates.
RAZI-FULL:v21p105/r2.anchor: كانا أخوين في بني إسرائيل أحدهما كافر اسمه براطوس والآخر مؤمن اسمه يهوذا

RAZI-FULL:v21p105/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p105/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v21p105/r3.claim: Another view identifies the pair with the companion in al-Saffat who says, ‘I had a companion.’
RAZI-FULL:v21p105/r3.anchor: وقيل هما المذكوران في سورة الصافات

RAZI-FULL:v21p105/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p105/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v21p105/r4.claim: A garden is called a jannah because its trees shade and conceal what lies beneath; the root means covering.
RAZI-FULL:v21p105/r4.anchor: وسمى البستان جنة لاستتار ما يستتر فيها بظل الأشجار

RAZI-FULL:v21p105/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p105/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v21p105/r5.claim: Palms encircle the gardens as angels encircle the Throne; hifaf means sides and ahifah its plural.
RAZI-FULL:v21p105/r5.anchor: أي وجعلنا النخل محيطا بالجنتين نظيره قوله تعالى

RAZI-FULL:v21p105/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p105/r6.speaker: الشاعر
RAZI-FULL:v21p105/r6.claim: The line about glances at the sides of a couch attests to hifaf meaning sides or surrounding edges.
RAZI-FULL:v21p105/r6.anchor: قال الشاعر : له لحظات في حفافي سريره

RAZI-FULL:v21p106/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p106/r1.speaker: صاحب الكشاف
RAZI-FULL:v21p106/r1.claim: Al-Zamakhshari says circling someone takes one object, with bi adding a second; farmers also favor fruit trees around vineyards for beauty.
RAZI-FULL:v21p106/r1.anchor: قال صاحب ( الكشاف ) : حفوه إذا طافوا به

RAZI-FULL:v21p106/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p106/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v21p106/r2.claim: Crops between the gardens provide staples and fruits, occupy a broad uninterrupted tract, and yield successive benefits at different times.
RAZI-FULL:v21p106/r2.anchor: أن تكون تلك الأرض جامعة للأقوات والفواكه

STUDYQURAN:18:32/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:18:32/r1.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:18:32/r1.claim: The parable follows the prominent Makkans' refusal to sit with followers they deemed socially inferior; it warns that prideful ingratitude for worldly blessings ends in their loss.
STUDYQURAN:18:32/r1.anchor: follows the discussion of the prominent and wealthy Makkans’ aversion to sitting with those of the Prophet’s followers

STUDYQURAN:18:32/r2.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:18:32/r2.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:18:32/r2.claim: The parable's gardens resemble the date-palm and grapevine garden with streams that the Makkans demanded as a condition of believing in the Prophet.
STUDYQURAN:18:32/r2.anchor: the gardens as described in this parable are similar to those the Makkans challenged the Prophet to bring forth

STUDYQURAN:18:32/r3.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:18:32/r3.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:18:32/r3.claim: Grapevines and date palms symbolize both worldly prosperity and Divine Beneficence in the Quran.
STUDYQURAN:18:32/r3.anchor: Gardens of grapevines and date palms are emblematic in the Quran of worldly prosperity but also Divine Beneficence

STUDYQURAN:18:32/r4.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:18:32/r4.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:18:32/r4.claim: Some reports identify the men as brothers, either Israelites or members of Makhzūm in Makkah; one disbelieving brother invested his inheritance in worldly goods, while the believing brother gave his away in charity.
STUDYQURAN:18:32/r4.anchor: Some reports say that the two men were brothers—either two Israelites or two brothers among the Makhzūm clan in Makkah

STUDYQURAN:18:32/r5.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:18:32/r5.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:18:32/r5.claim: Some commentators identify these brothers with the two men debating resurrection in 37:51–60.
STUDYQURAN:18:32/r5.anchor: Some commentators suggest that these two brothers are the same two debating resurrection

NAHHAS:v2p455/r9.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v2p455/r9.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v2p455/r9.claim: The underlying construction is ‘an example, the likeness of two men.’
NAHHAS:v2p455/r9.anchor: ^ ( واضرب لهم مثلا رجلين . . . . ) ^ [ 32 ] التقدير مثلا مثل الرجلين

TABATABAI:18:32-34/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:18:32-34/r2.speaker: بعض المفسرين
TABATABAI:18:32-34/r2.claim: Some commentators treat the two-garden story as an imagined example whose events need not have occurred.
TABATABAI:18:32-34/r2.anchor: ذكر بعض المفسرين أن الذي يتضمنه المثل قصة مقدرة مفروضة فليس من الواجب أن يتحقق مضمون المثل خارجا

TABATABAI:18:32-34/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:18:32-34/r3.speaker: آخرون
TABATABAI:18:32-34/r3.claim: Other commentators regard the garden story as a real event and transmit many conflicting accounts that the author says are unreliable.
TABATABAI:18:32-34/r3.anchor: وذكر آخرون أنه قصة واقعة، وقد رووا في ذلك قصصا كثيرة مختلفة لا معول عليها

TABATABAI:18:32-34/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:18:32-34/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:18:32-34/r4.claim: The two gardens, grapevines, surrounding palms, and crop between them support reading the story as an actual event.
TABATABAI:18:32-34/r4.anchor: غير أن التدبر في سياق القصة بما فيها من كونهما جنتين اثنتين

TABATABAI:18:32-34/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:18:32-34/r5.speaker: author
TABATABAI:18:32-34/r5.claim: The gardens are vineyards; fruit can name its tree, palms encircle both gardens, and the crop between them completes the cultivated food supply.
TABATABAI:18:32-34/r5.anchor: أي من كروم فالثمرة كثيرا ما يطلق على شجرتها

TABRISI:18:32-33/r1.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:18:32-33/r1.speaker: author
TABRISI:18:32-33/r1.claim: Ṭarafa's verse illustrates ḥafāf for the sides enclosing a winged object.
TABRISI:18:32-33/r1.anchor: كأن جناحي مضرحي تكنفا حفافيه شكا في العسيب بمسرد

TABRISI:18:32-33/r4.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:18:32-33/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
TABRISI:18:32-33/r4.claim: The two men were sons of an Israelite king who divided a great inheritance; the believer used his share to draw near to God, while the other bought estates including the gardens.
TABRISI:18:32-33/r4.anchor: يريد ابني ملك كان في بني إسرائيل توفي وترك ابنين وترك مالا جزيلا

TABRISI:18:32-33/r5.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:18:32-33/r5.speaker: علي بن إبراهيم
TABRISI:18:32-33/r5.claim: The parable is about a rich man with two large gardens and a poor neighbor; the author says this better fits the apparent wording.
TABRISI:18:32-33/r5.anchor: وفي تفسير علي بن إبراهيم بن هاشم أنه يريد رجلا كان له بستانان كبيران

THALABI:v6p169/r1.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p169/r1.speaker: author
THALABI:v6p169/r1.claim: The syntax makes ‘two men’ the object, with an implied comparison: ‘set out for them a parable like two men.’
THALABI:v6p169/r1.anchor: رجلين منصوب مفعول، على معنى: واضرب لهم مثلا كمثل رجلين.

THALABI:v6p169/r2.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p169/r2.speaker: author
THALABI:v6p169/r2.claim: Identifications differ: Meccan brothers Abu Salama and al-Aswad; Muhammad and Meccan polytheists; Uyayna ibn Hisn and companions compared with Salman and companions; or Israelite brothers with differing names reported for the believer and unbeliever.
THALABI:v6p169/r2.anchor: نزلت في أخوين من أهل مكة من بني مخزوم، أحدهما مؤمن وهو أبو سلمة

THALABI:v6p169/r3.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p169/r3.speaker: عطاء الخراساني
THALABI:v6p169/r3.claim: He tells of brothers sharing eight thousand dinars: one gave away a thousand each time the other bought worldly land, a house, wife, or servants, seeking the equivalent in Paradise.
THALABI:v6p169/r3.anchor: معمر عن عطاء الخراساني قال: كان رجلان شريكين، وكان لهما ثمانية آلاف دينار،

THALABI:v6p170/r1.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p170/r1.speaker: عطاء الخراساني
THALABI:v6p170/r1.claim: After giving away his share, the believer became needy and asked his wealthy brother for help; the brother rejected him and denied resurrection and recompense. The account links to 37:50–57.
THALABI:v6p170/r1.anchor: ثم أصابته حاجة شديدة فقال: لو أتيت صاحبي هذا لعله ينالني منه معروف.

THALABI:v6p170/r2.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p170/r2.speaker: author
THALABI:v6p170/r2.claim: The vineyards were surrounded by palms, with crops between them.
THALABI:v6p170/r2.anchor: بستانين من أعناب وحففناهما: أحطناهما بنخل وجعلنا بينهما زرعا،

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p7/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p7/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p7/r1.claim: In Ata's report, the two men are sons of an Israelite king: one built worldly palaces and gardens, while his ascetic brother spent equivalent wealth on the afterlife until it ran out; they exemplify the believer and the disbeliever made insolent by blessing.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p7/r1.anchor: قال ابن عباس في رواية عطاء: (يريد ابني ملك كان في بني

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p7/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p7/r2.speaker: الكلبي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p7/r2.claim: Al-Kalbi identifies the pair as brothers from Banu Makhzum: the believer Abu Salama, husband of Umm Salama, and the disbeliever al-Aswad.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p7/r2.anchor: وقال الكلبي: (هما أخوان من بني مخزوم

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p7/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p7/r3.speaker: أبو إسحاق
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p7/r3.claim: Abu Ishaq says polytheists, advised by Jews, asked about the Cave Companions, the Spirit, and these two men; God answered with parables for the Prophet, disbelievers, believers, and those who turned away from God.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p7/r3.anchor: قال أبو إسحاق: (كان المشركون سألوا النبي

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p7/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p7/r4.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p7/r4.claim: The phrase 'a parable of two men' is accusative as the object of ضرب.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p7/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p7/r5.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p7/r5.claim: Ḥaff means to surround: the palms were placed all around the two gardens; the same root appears for angels surrounding the Throne.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p7/r5.anchor: الحف: الإطافة بالشيء، يقال: حف القوم بسيدهم يحفون

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p7/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p7/r6.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p7/r6.claim: The crops were placed between the gardens; the report then describes the gardens as complete in their fruit, grapes, and crops.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p7/r6.anchor: والمعنى: جعلنا النخل مطبقا بها {وجعلنا بينهما} أي: بين الجنتين {زرعا}

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:18:32/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:18:32/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:18:32/r1.claim: The two men were sons of a deceased Israelite king: one built palaces and gardens, while the other renounced worldly life and sought the Hereafter.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:18:32/r1.anchor: يعني: ابني ملك كان في بني إسرائيل توفي وتركهما، فاتخذ أحدهما القصور والأجنة، والآخر كان زاهدا في الدنيا، راغبا في الآخرة

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:18:32/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:18:32/r2.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:18:32/r2.claim: Whenever the worldly brother acquired adornment, the ascetic gave its counterpart for his Hereafter, building gardens and palaces with God until his wealth ran out.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:18:32/r2.anchor: فكان إذا عمل أخوه شيئا من زينة الدنيا، أخذ الزاهد مثل ذلك، فقدمه لآخرته، واتخذ به عند الله الأجنة والقصور حتى نفد ماله

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:18:32/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:18:32/r3.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:18:32/r3.claim: The parable represents a believer and an unbeliever made insolent by prosperity.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:18:32/r3.anchor: فضربهما الله مثلا للمؤمن والكافر الذي أبطرته النعمة

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:18:32/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:18:32/r4.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:18:32/r4.claim: The two gardens had grapevines, palms surrounding them, and crops between them.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:18:32/r4.anchor: { جعلنا لأحدهما جنتين من أعناب وحففناهما بنخل } وجعلنا النخل مطبقا بهما { وجعلنا بينهما } بين الجنتين { زرعا }

SAMIN-DURR:18:32/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:18:32/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:18:32/r1.claim: In ḍaraba mathalan, ḍaraba may take two objects, as discussed in al-Baqara; Abū al-Baqāʾ parses an omitted mathal mithla rajulayni, with jaʿalnā explaining mathal, or takes it as an accusative adjective of rajulayni.
SAMIN-DURR:18:32/r1.anchor: قد تقدم أن " ضرب " مع المثل، يجوز أن يتعدى لاثنين في سورة البقرة.

SAMIN-DURR:18:32/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:18:32/r2.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:18:32/r2.claim: Ḥaffa bi-shayʾ means to surround it on every side; the Nābigha’s line uses it for encircling. Ḥaffa people means they made a ring around it, and ḥaffaftuhu bihi means I made it surrounded by it.
SAMIN-DURR:18:32/r2.anchor: وحففناهما } يقال: حف بالشيء: طاف به من جميع جوانبه، قال النابغة:

ZAJJAJ:v3p283/r6.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v3p283/r6.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v3p283/r6.claim: The Meccan polytheists, advised by Jews, asked Muhammad about the Cave Companions, the Spirit, and the two men; God made the parable an example for the Prophet, unbelievers, believers, and deniers.
ZAJJAJ:v3p283/r6.anchor: كان المشركون سألوا النبي - صلى الله عليه وسلم - بمشورة إليهود عليهم أن يسألوا النبي - صلى الله عليه وسلم

ZAJJAJ:v3p283/r7.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v3p283/r7.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v3p283/r7.claim: Rajalayn is accusative as the object implied by the command to strike a parable: the parable of two men.
ZAJJAJ:v3p283/r7.anchor:
(رجلين) منصوب على معنى المفعول على معنى واضرب لهم مثلا مثل
رجلين.

ZAJJAJ:v3p283/r8.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v3p283/r8.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v3p283/r8.claim: The palms were set around the two gardens; Arabic uses ḥaffa for people surrounding someone, as in ḥaffa al-qawmu bi-Zayd.
ZAJJAJ:v3p283/r8.anchor:
(وحففناها بنخل) أي جعلنا النخل مطيفا بهما، يقال: قد حف القوم
بزيد

ZAJJAJ:v3p283/r9.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v3p283/r9.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v3p283/r9.claim: The gardens’ cultivation was complete and continuous, and both fully produced from their palms, grapes, and intervening crops.
ZAJJAJ:v3p283/r9.anchor: فأعلم الله أن عمارتهما كاملة متصلة لا يفصل بينهما إلا عمارة

ASAD-NOTES:18:32#n42/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:18:32#n42/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:18:32#n42/r1.claim: The garden parable connects with 18:7-8 and illustrates that earthly beauty is a means by which God tests people.
ASAD-NOTES:18:32#n42/r1.anchor: This parable connects with verses 7-8 of this surah, and serves as an illustration of the statement that "all beauty on earth is a means by which God puts men to a test"

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p173/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p173/r9.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p173/r9.claim: The parable addresses arrogant leaders who wanted poor believers expelled; the rich unbeliever mirrors them, while the poor believer mirrors the faithful, showing wealth can vanish and obedience is the true honor.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p173/r9.anchor: والضمير في لهم عائد على المتجبرين الطالبين من الرسول صلى الله عليه وسلم طرد الضعفاء

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p173/r10.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p173/r10.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p173/r10.claim: The parable connects to the preceding debate about wealth and supporters, and واضرب مثلا means recount the story; جعلنا may explain the parable or describe the two men.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p173/r10.anchor: وظهر بضرب هذا المثل الربط بين هذه الآية والتي قبلها

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p173/r13.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p173/r13.speaker: ابن عطية
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p173/r13.claim: Ibn Atiyya praises the construction as an unsurpassed worldly estate: paired grape gardens ringed by palms, with a cultivated space and a river irrigating all.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p173/r13.anchor: قال ابن عطية: وتأمل هذه الهيئة التي ذكر الله فإن المرء لا يكاد يتخيل أجل منهما

TAB-FULL:v1p35/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p35/r1.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
TAB-FULL:v1p35/r1.claim: At Adhāt Banī Ghifār, Gabriel successively conveyed commands to recite on one, two, three, then seven aḥruf; the Prophet sought relief for his community, and said any of the seven is correct.
TAB-FULL:v1p35/r1.anchor: أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم، كان عند أضاة بني غفار

TAB-FULL:v1p35/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p35/r2.speaker: أبي بن كعب
TAB-FULL:v1p35/r2.claim: Ubayy heard two men recite Sūrat al-Naḥl differently; each said the Prophet had taught him his reading.
TAB-FULL:v1p35/r2.anchor: عن أبي بن كعب، أنه قال: سمعت رجلا، يقرأ في سورة النحل قراءة تخالف قراءتي، ثم سمعت آخر

TAB-FULL:v1p35/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p35/r3.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
TAB-FULL:v1p35/r3.claim: The Prophet asked each man to recite and affirmed both readings as good, calming Ubayy's distress at the differences.
TAB-FULL:v1p35/r3.anchor: فقال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم لأحدهما: «اقرأ»

TAB-FULL:v1p35/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p35/r4.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
TAB-FULL:v1p35/r4.claim: When Ubayy reddened with demonic misgivings, the Prophet touched his chest and prayed for Satan to be driven away from him.
TAB-FULL:v1p35/r4.anchor: فعرف ذلك رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم في وجهي، فضرب بيده في صدري

TAB-FULL:v1p35/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p35/r5.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
TAB-FULL:v1p35/r5.claim: The Prophet says God granted seven aḥruf and a request with each successive command; he asked forgiveness for his community and reserved his third intercession for Judgment Day.
TAB-FULL:v1p35/r5.anchor: فقال: إن الله يأمرك أن تقرأ القرآن على سبعة أحرف، ولك بكل ردة مسألة

TAB-FULL:v1p37/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p37/r1.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
TAB-FULL:v1p37/r1.claim: The Prophet accepted two men’s differing recitations, then Ubayy’s, affirming each as correct after they said he had taught it.
TAB-FULL:v1p37/r1.anchor: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم، فقال: يا نبي الله، اختلفنا في آية من القرآن

TAB-FULL:v1p37/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p37/r2.speaker: أبي
TAB-FULL:v1p37/r2.claim: Ubayy recounts that permission expanded from one letter to seven after repeated requests for ease; each reading carried a supplication, with a final intercession reserved for his community.
TAB-FULL:v1p37/r2.anchor: قال أبي: فدخلني من الشك في أمر رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم ما دخل في من أمر الجاهلية

TAB-FULL:v1p37/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p37/r3.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
TAB-FULL:v1p37/r3.claim: Abu Bakra reports Gabriel asked for one letter and Michael for more, until six or seven; all suffice provided mercy and punishment verses are not exchanged, like come and approach.
TAB-FULL:v1p37/r3.anchor: عن أبيه، قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم

BAQILLANI:v1p294/r1.author: al-Bāqillānī
BAQILLANI:v1p294/r1.speaker: author
BAQILLANI:v1p294/r1.claim: Opponents wrongly explain the Qurʾān’s inimitability as the Messenger’s privileged knowledge of composition, which others lack; on that account they cannot distinguish divine from prophetic authorship.
BAQILLANI:v1p294/r1.anchor: لأن مذهبهم أنه لا فرق بين أن يكون القرآن من قبل الرسول أو من قبل الله عز وجل في كونه معجزا

BAQILLANI:v1p294/r2.author: al-Bāqillānī
BAQILLANI:v1p294/r2.speaker: author
BAQILLANI:v1p294/r2.claim: Bāqillānī locates the obstacle in inability to produce Qurʾānic composition, not merely in lacking knowledge of how it is composed.
BAQILLANI:v1p294/r2.anchor: وقد بينا قبل هذا أن المانع هو أنهم لا يقدرون عليه

BAQILLANI:v1p294/r3.author: al-Bāqillānī
BAQILLANI:v1p294/r3.speaker: author
BAQILLANI:v1p294/r3.claim: Knowing a craft’s rules does not ensure equal performance: people may know meters, eloquence, weaving, or archery yet differ in natural ability and execution.
BAQILLANI:v1p294/r3.anchor: وكذلك أهل نظم الكلام يتفاضلون مع العلم بكيفية النظم وكذلك أهل الرمي يتفاضلون في الإصابة مع العلم بكيفية الإصابة

BAQILLANI:v1p294/r4.author: al-Bāqillānī
BAQILLANI:v1p294/r4.speaker: author
BAQILLANI:v1p294/r4.claim: One exceptional line better than Imruʾ al-Qays does not prove its poet knows composition better; if knowledge were decisive, the poet’s whole body of work would match that level.
BAQILLANI:v1p294/r4.anchor: وإذا وجدت للشاعر بيتا أو قطعة أحسن من شعر امرئ القيس لم يدل ذلك على أنه أعلم بالنظم منه

BAQILLANI:v1p294/r5.author: al-Bāqillānī
BAQILLANI:v1p294/r5.speaker: author
BAQILLANI:v1p294/r5.claim: A person may know how to write yet be unable to reproduce an existing line exactly, showing that knowledge can remain while capacity fails.
BAQILLANI:v1p294/r5.anchor: وهذا يبين لك بأنه قد يعلم الخط فيكتب سطرا فلو أراد أن يأتي بمثله بحيث لا يغادر منه شيئا لتعذر والعلم حاصل

BURHAN:v3p6/r1.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v3p6/r1.speaker: الفراء
BURHAN:v3p6/r1.claim: Al-Farra says God addresses a human interlocutor in the dual; some take the two gardens in 18:32 as one combined garden, citing the singular دخل جنته in 18:35.
BURHAN:v3p6/r1.anchor: قال يخاطب الإنسان مخاطبه بالتثنية وجعل منه

ITQAN:v4p339/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v4p339/r1.speaker: author
ITQAN:v4p339/r1.claim: The Qur’an contains stories of the People of the Cave, the Inscription, Nebuchadnezzar, the two men and their gardens, the Garden people, the believer of Ya-Sin, and the Elephant.
ITQAN:v4p339/r1.anchor: وقصة أصحاب الكهف وقصة أصحاب الرقيم وقصة بخت نصر وقصة الرجلين اللذين لأحدهما الجنة وقصة أصحاب الجنة

ITQAN:v4p339/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v4p339/r2.speaker: author
ITQAN:v4p339/r2.claim: It recounts the Prophet’s call, glad tidings, mission, migration, battles, family events, the Slander, the Night Journey, the splitting of the moon, and the Jews’ sorcery against him.
ITQAN:v4p339/r2.anchor: وفيه من شأن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم دعوة إبراهيم به وبشارة عيسى وبعثه وهجرته ومن غزواته سرية ابن الحضرمي

ITQAN:v4p339/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v4p339/r3.speaker: author
ITQAN:v4p339/r3.claim: The Qur’an describes human creation and death, the soul and grave, the signs of the Hour, resurrection, gathering, judgment, testimony, books, intercession, Paradise and its delights, and Hell and its punishments.
ITQAN:v4p339/r3.anchor: وفيه بدء خلق الإنسان إلى موته وكيفية الموت وقبض الروح وما يفعل بها بعد وصعودها إلى السماء وفتح الباب للمؤمنة

ITQAN:v4p339/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v4p339/r4.speaker: author
ITQAN:v4p339/r4.claim: It contains all God’s beautiful names as reported in a hadith, along with many of the Prophet’s names.
ITQAN:v4p339/r4.anchor: وفيه جميع أسمائه تعالى الحسنى كما ورد في حديث ومن أسمائه مطلقا ألف اسم ومن أسماء النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم جملة

ITQAN:v4p339/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v4p339/r5.speaker: author
ITQAN:v4p339/r5.claim: It includes the branches of faith and the laws of Islam.
ITQAN:v4p339/r5.anchor: وفي شعب الإيمان البضع والسبعون وشرائع الإسلام الثلاثمائة وخمسة عشر

ITQAN:v4p339/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v4p339/r6.speaker: author
ITQAN:v4p339/r6.claim: The Qur’an includes the categories of major sins and many minor sins.
ITQAN:v4p339/r6.anchor: وفيه أنواع الكبائر وكثير من الصغائر

ITQAN:v4p339/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v4p339/r7.speaker: author
ITQAN:v4p339/r7.claim: The Qur’an confirms every report transmitted from the Prophet, among many other subjects requiring extensive explanation.
ITQAN:v4p339/r7.anchor: وفيه تصديق كل حديث ورد عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم إلى غير ذلك مما يحتاج شرحه إلى مجلدات

JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p173/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p173/r1.speaker: author
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p173/r1.claim: A generic red rose is an inadequate counterpart when the intended flower has white around its red center; the compared image must share that defining condition.
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p173/r1.anchor: تشبيه الورد الأحمر بالخد فإنه يفسد من حيث إن المصد إلى جنس من الورد مخصوص

JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p173/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p173/r2.speaker: author
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p173/r2.claim: In a multi-part simile, one comparison may be placed as a dependent description of the other instead of being coordinated with it, as in the line about gray hair rising in youth.
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p173/r2.anchor: تجد أحد المشبهين في الأمر الأعم الأكثر وقد ذكر في صلة الآخر ولم يعطف عليه

JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p173/r3.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p173/r3.speaker: author
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p173/r3.claim: When waw introduces a circumstantial clause, that clause remains subordinate like an adjective; the Mars-and-Jupiter example makes the second image dependent on the first.
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p173/r3.anchor: فإن جاءت الواو كانت واو حال كقوله

JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p173/r4.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p173/r4.speaker: author
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p173/r4.claim: Stars falling are grammatically a description of night, so they remain subordinate; likewise the night is described as having day call at its sides.
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p173/r4.anchor: قوله ليل تهاوي كواكبه فتهاوى كواكبه جملة من الصفة لليل

JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p173/r5.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p173/r5.speaker: author
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p173/r5.claim: Imru al-Qays's paired dates are an exception: the two items are coordinated on both sides, and a plural such as 'hearts' does not make one item subordinate to another.
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p173/r5.anchor: وبيت امرئ القيس على خلاف هذه الطريقة لأن أحد الشيئين فيه في الطرفين معطوف على الآخر

JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p173/r6.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p173/r6.speaker: author
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p173/r6.claim: In the Imru al-Qays example the explicit coordination is in the predicate, 'fresh and dry'; the plural form on the subject similarly encompasses distinct equal items.
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p173/r6.anchor: هذا وقد صرح بالعطف في البدل وهو المقصود فقال رطبا ويابسا

JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p173/r7.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p173/r7.speaker: author
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p173/r7.claim: The line about the speaker adorning a company with praise compares only the act of praise to hanging a pearl on a pig: praise is wasted on those unable to benefit from adornment.
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p173/r7.anchor: إني وتزييني بمدحي معشرا كمعلق درا على خنزير

JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p173/r8.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p173/r8.speaker: author
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p173/r8.claim: That comparison concerns the whole act with its complement, not hanging by itself; waw means 'with' because there are no two parallel predicates to coordinate.
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p173/r8.anchor: فالشبه مأخوذ من مجموع المصدر وما في صلته ولا بد للواو في هذا النحو أن تكون بمعنى مع

JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p175/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p175/r1.speaker: author
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p175/r1.claim: Unlike fa, thumma, and aw, wāw adds no sequence, delay, or alternative; it only joins elements under the grammatical relation they share.
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p175/r1.anchor: وليس للواو معنى سوى الإشراك في الحكم الذي يقتضيه الإعراب

JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p175/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p175/r2.speaker: author
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p175/r2.claim: Coordinated clauses need a meaningful relation: saying Zayd stands and ʿAmr sits presumes that ʿAmr is connected to Zayd and that the listener cares to learn his state too.
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p175/r2.anchor: ليس منه بسبب ولا هو مما يذكر بذكره ويتصل حديثه بحديثه

JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p175/r3.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p175/r3.speaker: author
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p175/r3.claim: Joining a clause unrelated to its predecessor makes the sentence absurd, as in the example of leaving home and then praising a poet with no connection.
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p175/r3.anchor: فلو قلت : خرجت اليوم من داري . ثم قلت : وأحسن الذي يقول بيت كذا . قلت ما يضحك منه

KHATTABI:v1p62/r1.author: al-Khaṭṭābī
KHATTABI:v1p62/r1.speaker: author
KHATTABI:v1p62/r1.claim: The opening of al-Nābigha’s poem is exceptionally beautiful and eloquently conveys distress and a long, sleepless night; it was said no poet began better.
KHATTABI:v1p62/r1.anchor: متناه في الحسن , بليغ في وصف ما شكاه , من همه وطول ليله

KHATTABI:v1p62/r2.author: al-Khaṭṭābī
KHATTABI:v1p62/r2.speaker: author
KHATTABI:v1p62/r2.claim: The image of a chest relieved by night borrows from a shepherd settling camels at their nighttime resting place; its natural ease joins eloquence and sweetness.
KHATTABI:v1p62/r2.anchor: وصدر أراح الليل عزب همه مستعار من إراحة الراعي الإبل إلى مباتها

KHATTABI:v1p62/r3.author: al-Khaṭṭābī
KHATTABI:v1p62/r3.speaker: author
KHATTABI:v1p62/r3.claim: Al-Nābigha’s lines are accomplished, but al-Imruʾ al-Qays surpasses them in crafted technique, simile, and inventive meanings.
KHATTABI:v1p62/r3.anchor: إلا أن في أبيات امرئ القيس من ثقافة الصنعة وحسن التشبيه وإبداع المعاني ما ليس في أبيات النابغة

KHATTABI:v1p62/r4.author: al-Khaṭṭābī
KHATTABI:v1p62/r4.speaker: author
KHATTABI:v1p62/r4.claim: Al-Imruʾ al-Qays gives night a body and compares gathering darkness to successive, colliding sea waves.
KHATTABI:v1p62/r4.anchor: جعل لليل صلبا وأعجازا وكلكلا , وشبه تراكم ظلمة الليل بموج البحر

KHATTABI:v1p62/r5.author: al-Khaṭṭābī
KHATTABI:v1p62/r5.speaker: author
KHATTABI:v1p62/r5.claim: He depicts the stars as firmly rope-bound, motionless, and unable to depart, intensifying the night’s oppressive stillness.
KHATTABI:v1p62/r5.anchor: وجعل النجوم كأنها مشدودة بحبال وثيقة فهي راكدة لا تزول ولا تبرح

KHATTABI:v1p62/r6.author: al-Khaṭṭābī
KHATTABI:v1p62/r6.speaker: author
KHATTABI:v1p62/r6.claim: The poem first longs for dawn as relief, then reverses course: the affliction is too great for any time to end or cure it.
KHATTABI:v1p62/r6.anchor: فزعم أن البلوى أعظم من أن يكون لها في شيء من الأوقات كشف وانجلاء

KHATTABI:v1p62/r7.author: al-Khaṭṭābī
KHATTABI:v1p62/r7.speaker: الشعبي
KHATTABI:v1p62/r7.claim: The report says al-Walīd stamped his foot while hearing the poem, and al-Shaʿbī declared the matter settled, signaling recognition of al-Imruʾ al-Qays’s excellence.
KHATTABI:v1p62/r7.anchor: قال فركض الوليد برجله , فقال الشعبي: بانت القضية

KHATTABI:v1p62/r8.author: al-Khaṭṭābī
KHATTABI:v1p62/r8.speaker: author
KHATTABI:v1p62/r8.claim: A comparison of competing poems distinguishes their levels by deciding whether one leads, the other falls short, or they are equal.
KHATTABI:v1p62/r8.anchor: فبمثل هذه الأمور تعتبر معاني المعارضة فيقع بها الفصل بين الكلامين

KHATTABI:v1p63/r1.author: al-Khaṭṭābī
KHATTABI:v1p63/r1.speaker: author
KHATTABI:v1p63/r1.claim: When poets share a subject, one can reach its summit while the other falls short; al-Aʿshā’s treatment of wine outdoes al-Akhṭal’s.
KHATTABI:v1p63/r1.anchor: فيرتقي أحدهما إلى ذروته ويقصر شأو الآخر عن مساواته في درجته , كالأعشى والأخطل

KHATTABI:v1p63/r2.author: al-Khaṭṭābī
KHATTABI:v1p63/r2.speaker: هشام ابن أدهم المازني
KHATTABI:v1p63/r2.claim: Hishām reports that al-Shaʿbī visited a drunken al-Akhṭal, who boasted of his wine verse; al-Shaʿbī preferred al-Aʿshā’s verse, and al-Akhṭal conceded.
KHATTABI:v1p63/r2.anchor: هشام ابن أدهم المازني -وكان علامة - قال: دخل الشعبي على الأخطل

KHATTABI:v1p63/r3.author: al-Khaṭṭābī
KHATTABI:v1p63/r3.speaker: author
KHATTABI:v1p63/r3.claim: Al-Akhṭal says the wine’s aroma reaches a person with a cold, whereas al-Aʿshā makes its sharp aroma dispel congestion and cure the ailment, a stronger image.
KHATTABI:v1p63/r3.anchor: وقد طبت لدائه وتأيت لبرئه وشفائه

KHATTABI:v1p63/r4.author: al-Khaṭṭābī
KHATTABI:v1p63/r4.speaker: author
KHATTABI:v1p63/r4.claim: A more striking form of poetic contest builds something up and then demolishes it, or establishes an idea before reversing it.
KHATTABI:v1p63/r4.anchor: بناء الشيء وهدمه , وتشييده ثم وضعه ونقضه

KHATTABI:v1p63/r5.author: al-Khaṭṭābī
KHATTABI:v1p63/r5.speaker: حسان بن ثابت
KHATTABI:v1p63/r5.claim: Jabala asked Ḥassān to disparage wine because it had captivated him; Ḥassān began a verse saying the cup would otherwise be worth nothing to its drinker.
KHATTABI:v1p63/r5.anchor: قال حسان: أتيت جبلة بني الأيهم الغساني وقد مدحته فقال لي: يا أبا الوليد

DAMGHANI:v1p191/r15.author: al-Dāmghānī
DAMGHANI:v1p191/r15.speaker: author
DAMGHANI:v1p191/r15.claim: The two men in the parable are Israelites; their story is well known.
